correctness.rationale: Convexity of metric functionals gives weak lower semicontinuity and hence the upper topology inclusion; Walsh's extreme-dual metric functionals give the lower inclusion. Supporting functionals produce finite-codimensional subspaces in basic neighborhoods. On C(K), pairwise disjoint bump supports force every internal, and hence every limiting, metric functional to be negative on at most one bump, proving d-weak convergence for arbitrary prescribed amplitudes.

originality.rationale: The recent topology paper proves only coarseness relative to the metric topology and a C[0,1] counterexample. The older weak-convergence paper and Walsh supply ingredients but do not state the topology sandwich, finite-dimensional topology equality, finite-codimensional neighborhood theorem, or the exact finite-versus-infinite C(K) dichotomy located here. The C(K) extension remains close enough to the recent disjoint-support construction that parallel or future coverage is a material residual risk.

value.rationale: The result directly locates the new metric-functional topology among classical Banach-space topologies, upgrades sequential facts to topology-level equalities for broad classes, and shows that arbitrary norm growth of d-weak null sequences is universal across infinite compact-Hausdorff C(K) spaces rather than peculiar to C[0,1].
